title: Abelian untensored base change for arbitrary affine schemes
statement: Let K be a field, Z an affine K-scheme, S′ a K-scheme, and g:T→S′ a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism. For every abelian sheaf A on the small etale site of T whose geometric-stalk elements have finite order invertible in K [def-kun-torsion-invertible], the canonical bounded-below derived exchange (Z×_K S′→S′)^* Rg_* A[0] → R(pullback.fst)_* (pullback.snd)^* A[0] is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. No finite-type condition is imposed on Z.

source.place: Tags 0F1I and 0EZT, arbitrary-scheme reduction in Tag 0F1J

proof.text: Give the coordinate algebra B of Z its K-algebra structure from z. The finitely generated K-subalgebras form a nonempty directed set with union B. Use the source library’s CommRingCat.isColimitFGSubalgebraCocone to obtain the actual ring colimit; Spec preserves the opposite limit. Extend this limit cone across the canonical affine isomorphism Z ≅ Spec B. The structure maps to Spec K commute with its projections by naturality of isoSpec. Each stage is finite type over K.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, assertion (2)

proof.text: Build the systems X_i=Z_i×_K S′ and Y_i=X_i×_{S′}T using pointwise pullbacks. Construct their limit cones directly: their universal lifts are pullback lifts of the three limit lifts, and uniqueness follows by both pullback projections and limit hom-ext. Their transition morphisms are affine by the affine fibre-product transition lemma.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, assertion (2)

proof.text: Apply finite-type field base change to each Z_i and A. Identify its unbounded exchange with the bounded-below exchange, cancel the endpoint comparison isomorphisms, and reflect invertibility along the full inclusion D+ into D.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, assertion (2)

proof.text: Apply continuity of higher direct images in each nonnegative degree. The S′ and T diagrams are constant with identity transitions. Their limit cones use the connectedness of a nonempty directed index, and the coefficient cocone is the identity after the inverse-image identity isomorphism. Verify its unit and composition coherence using upperStarComp_id_right and naturality; this identifies the canonical maps, not just the endpoints. Stalkwise finite order implies A.IsTorsion. Thus the degree-q exchange at the limit is invertible. Negative cohomology of both endpoints vanishes by left exactness and exact inverse image; the derived cohomology criterion proves invertibility.

theorem abelian_affineScheme_untensored_baseChange
    {K : Type u} [Field K] {Z S' T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Z]
    (z : Z ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [S'.Over (Spec (.of K))]
    (g : T ⟶ S') [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (A : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hA : IsTorsionOfInvertibleOrder K (Over.mk (g ≫ (S' ↘ Spec (.of K)))) A) :
    IsIso ((derivedBaseChangeMapPlus AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
      (CommSq.mk (pullback.condition
        (f := pullback.snd z (S' ↘ Spec (.of K))) (g := g)).symm)).app
      ((_root_.DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor
        (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) 0).obj A))
